Loop Tuner

An oscilloscope for control loops. The display shows the signals of the loop; you set the loop up in the tabs below, one step at a time: the Input tab makes the signals, the Plant tab wires the system as a block diagram, the Controller tab chooses and tunes its controllers, the Auto-tune tab improves them by simulation. Earlier runs stay faded on the display for five runs, so a change can be compared with before.

Display

RRun / Stop. Running sweeps the record at the speed set in the header (1×: real time), over and over. With an External plant, Run and Stop start and stop it. SSingle: one sweep, then stop. Pressed while running, the sweep under way finishes, then the scope stops. EE-STOP, with an External plant connected (also the red key in the header) HHold, while a live plant runs: the screen freezes, the plant and the live record go on AAuto Scale: fit the timebase and every channel to the data KnobsDrag, scroll, or focus and use the arrow keys. Double-click a Position knob to zero it. Click a readout to type a value (20m, 100 ms). Lit keysA key that is lit is on or chosen, everywhere on the page: the display mode, the open tab, the signal or variant you edit. Run/Stop is lit green while running and red while stopped; Single amber while it sweeps. Channel keysUnder Vertical and under the screen, the same keys: lit in the channel's colour while the channel is on. Press one to select it for the Vertical knobs (a bar under its number marks it); press the selected one again to turn it off WheelOn the plot: zoom time and values around the cursor. On the time axis or the value axis: that axis only. DragPan. Click a trace or its marker first to move and zoom that line alone; Esc releases it. Shift + dragZoom to the marked box; a flat band zooms time only, a narrow band values only SeparatorsDrag the gaps between display, controls and tabs to resize; double-click to reset MeasureVertical › Measure: a line under the screen for the selected channel with its mean, rms, ac rms, peak to peak, total variation per second (TV, how far it travels: an actuator's wear) and reversals per second (turns larger than a tenth of a division), over what the screen shows. A waveform with fewer than 10 samples per period is marked under-resolved: its rms is then wrong. Spectrogram levelsThe strip at the right edge: a histogram of the amplitudes shown (dB) beside the colour bar. Below the floor is black, above the ceiling the brightest colour. Drag a handle or the band between them; the wheel moves the floor, Shift + wheel the ceiling; double-click for automatic levels (the floor 10 dB above the median, the noise). Levels belong to the signal shown; Run Control › Levels types them (↑ ↓: 1 dB, Shift: 10 dB).

Speed, in the header, sets how fast simulated time runs: 1× is real time, 10× ten times faster, 0.1× slower; type any factor, or -1 or inf for ∞, as fast as possible. No speed runs faster than this page simulates the screen (timed after each change); ∞ runs at that, so it depends on the system and on the time per division (a finer screen takes more steps per second). Beside it, the speed achieved over the last second; its tooltip gives the simulation's speed. Auto-tune runs at it too. With a live plant connected it stays at 1× (a lock shows it): the plant owns the clock.

The screen is the record: what you see is simulated and swept, at that speed. Save ▾, under the screen, stores it: every signal as CSV or JSON, Screenshot (PNG) (the screen with its status line and channel keys), or Copy image to the clipboard. Open… shows a saved trace dashed on the channels with the same names, until you clear it (ref ✕); ◀ ▶ step through one longer than the screen.

Signal generator

Press a waveform key to draft a component: the display shows it dashed on its own and added to the signal. Adjust it, then Add. Click a component in the stack to edit it. The input repeats with its Period; Auto Scale shows one period. Function takes a formula in t, such as 0.3*sin(2*pi*4*t) + step(t-0.5).

0–9 . -Type a value for the active field; Enter sets it EnterWith nothing typed: add (or apply) the draft EscClear what you typed, or cancel the draft ← →Move the digit cursor ↑ ↓Change the digit under the cursor (the dial does the same) TabNext field Ctrl ZUndo; Ctrl Shift Z redo

Plant

The plant is a block diagram. Drag blocks in from the library (or click to add), drag from an output to an input to wire them, click a block to set its parameters on the right. Source blocks play a signal made in the Input tab; Sink blocks (x, speed, …) can be shown on any channel. Double-click a Controller block to open it in the Controller tab. Shift-drag or Shift-click to select several, Ctrl G to group them into a subsystem, double-click a subsystem to open it, Esc to go back up. A subsystem can be saved to My blocks. Double-click a Switch to move it to its next input. Wheel zooms the canvas; dragging the background pans.

An Equations block (Math) computes named outputs from named inputs, one line name = formula at a time; an Integrator may have a start value and limits (it stops at them: a tank overflows at its brim). A subsystem may carry a mask: parameters the blocks inside read by name, shown when it is selected; any number inside may then be a formula such as 1/k, shown with its value. The physics models are such subsystems: double-click the cart, the rods or the tank to open them. The carts are Mechanics parts (World, Rail, Hinge, Mass, Rod) joined at their frame ports, the small squares on their bottom edge: drag from one port to another to join them. Selecting a part shows the equations of motion, derived from how the parts are joined, in the names of the parameters; hover a coefficient for its value. When a run is stiff or needs attention, the line above the screen says so (all of it: loopTuner.info()).

A mask may hold switches (a key, on or off) and choices (a list), their fields folded under them. A switch that is off is not compiled: its blocks are drawn faint inside and its Sinks read nothing. The library's Components group holds the Servo motor: a DC motor with its drive (voltage or current), rotor, gear and encoder, its output shaft free (a load torque) or coupled (an elastic gear to an inertia outside, with backlash as a switch), and each non-ideality a switch on its mask (Coulomb friction, torque ripple and noise, the current loop, the supply limit, backlash, the encoder's coupling, angle errors, counts and delay, speed from the angle). The DC motor systems, the encoder example and Gear backlash use it. A component opens read-only and is saved as a reference with the values you set; Edit a copy makes it the project's own subsystem.

A plant can also have 2D views (Diagram | views above the canvas), set in the project's JSON: they move with the signals, following the scope's scan line (press Single for one run from t = 0) or your cursor. A robot has a 3D view drawn from its description (URDF): the arm posed by its joint angles, the reference path dashed and the tool's trail; drag to orbit, right-drag or Shift-drag to pan, the wheel zooms, W A S D Q E fly, the cube in the corner picks a view.

A wire may carry a vector (drawn double, with its count): Mux joins signals, Demux splits them, a Sink on it records one signal per element (q → q1 … q6). The Math blocks Matrix Gain, Product, Solve and Norm work on vectors and matrices, and the Robot group's blocks (forward kinematics, Jacobian, mass matrix, inverse dynamics, the damped inverse, frame transforms, joint limits) read the robot's URDF. Try PUMA 560, a circle in space.

Controller

A Controller block takes the reference r and the measurements, and drives the plant at its sample time Ts. It holds variants, implementations with the same inputs and output: click one to run it. Edit the running variant's parameters (the wheel over a number nudges it by 5 %, Shift 1 %; in a list such as Q, click into a value first), or add a variant from the library.

Variants from the plant (LQR, PI from the plant, PID + feedforward from the plant, swing-up with an LQR catch, the planned swing-up, and an Observer's Kalman filter) hold only inputs (weights, levels, times, limits and hand gains such as a feedforward or the swing-up's energy gain): their numbers are computed in the page from the plant as it is wired, every time it changes. The Computed box shows what was computed, from which plant, and why a design was refused (the block then puts out u = 0). A plan takes a few seconds and is made in the background: until it is ready the block puts out u = 0, or runs its previous plan, and the box shows the progress, with Cancel; the display then takes the new run from its start. Copy as numbers turns the numbers into a hand variant, which no longer follows the plant. Variants by hand: PID, state feedback, gain-scheduled PI, energy swing-up, relay (on/off), sliding mode, super-twisting; for an Observer, a Kalman filter on a model you give (for a plant the page cannot see), a Luenberger observer and finite differences. The sliding modes read the measured rate on input 3. A Controller with lanes runs one law per element of its vector inputs (the PUMA's six axis loops), each lane's numbers computed for that lane; its ff input adds a feedforward (the torque the arm's model says the motion takes) inside the limits. Speed PI from the plant puts each lane's speed loop at a bandwidth ω you choose. Try DC motor, sliding mode: its XY view is the phase portrait, and the line's slope λ sets how the error decays.

Auto-tune

Improves a Controller block's running variant by simulation, into a new variant (the original stays to compare). Iterate runs the loop again and again, keeping gains that lower the cost (IAE, ITAE or ISE of r − y, plus effort and overshoot beyond a bound): watch each improvement on the display and the cost fall in the plot. Relay makes the loop oscillate to find its ultimate gain and period, then applies a rule (Ziegler–Nichols, Tyreus–Luyben, no overshoot). Step response fits a lag and a dead time and tunes a PI by SIMC. Every run the tuner tries sweeps across the display at the header's Speed and lasts its own length, one period of the input, whatever the screen shows (a 5 s run takes 5 s at 1×, half a second at 10×); at ∞ it computes as fast as it can and shows each improvement. The scope's Stop stops the tuning too. One Ctrl Z undoes a whole run. Try it on Oven, badly tuned. A relay or step result that scores worse than what runs, or that is unstable where the run starts, is added but does not run. A variant from the plant is tuned as its Copy as numbers twin, from the numbers its design computes now, and the result is a hand variant beside it; a planned swing-up has no gains to tune (change its inputs in the Controller tab).

Analysis

The loop a Controller block closes, linearised from the plant it sees, with the running variant's own law: whether it is stable, its gain, phase and delay margins, Ms, the poles, root locus, Bode, Nyquist and the linear step, discrete at the block's Ts as it runs. At rest, Start or Scope time picks where it is linearised (the scope's time follows the cursor or the sweep). A law that has no linear model there (a relay, the ideal sliding mode, super-twisting, a swing-up pumping energy), a plan not made yet, or a plant outside the page is named, with the reason. A kink at that point (the empty tank at rest) has no slope to draw: it is refused, saying where to look instead. Where u sits at a limit, the linear loop does not hold: it says so first and grades nothing.

Live (HIL)

A system with an External plant block (Plant tab, group Live) runs against a plant outside the page, in real time; HIL: an external plant in the System library is made for it. Its plant, hil-plant.zip (Plant tab, Download the plant (zip)), stands in for real hardware: it simulates a model of the System library with this page's own code (by default a DC motor swinging an arm; --model NAME another, --list lists them, --random one at random), varies its physics by up to 15 % and switches its effects (friction, ripple, a resonance) at random, and tells the page only its inputs and outputs: the page has to identify it. Replace it with your device behind the same protocol, in any language. To run it, unzip it and run sh runme.sh (Linux, macOS) or double-click runme.cmd (Windows; it runs runme.ps1); they install what it needs (uv, which brings its own Python, websockets and the V8 engine that runs this page's code) and start it, in a window with a red STOP that also says where it listens. Then Connect in the Plant tab.

Nothing runs by itself. Offline the scope stands still and says OFFLINE. Connect opens the link and reads the plant's ports; the plant stays stopped. Run starts the plant and the sweep: first every reference moves to its waveform's first value at no more than 10 % of its full scale per second (the status line counts down), then the loop runs. Every channel spans its signal's full scale, for orientation. Stop stops both; Single runs one sweep and stops the plant (pressed while running, the sweep under way finishes first). Hold (H) freezes the screen while the plant runs on. Tune the controller meanwhile: a parameter takes effect at the next sample. A variant from the plant does not run against an External plant (the page has no model of a plant outside it): it puts out u = 0 and says why; a Kalman filter on a model you give does run.

E-STOP (the red key in the header, or E), STOP in the plant's window, or 10 silent cycles on either side stop it (safe inputs) until Reset: a STOP pressed at the plant is reset at the plant, the page's E-STOP on the page. The plant tells the page when it stops or starts at its own keys, and the page follows at once. In reference mode (Live settings, Mode: Plant, which asks the plant to switch while it is stopped; or start it as sh runme.sh --mode reference) the plant runs its model's own controller and the page sends the references: the page's controllers and Auto-tune are not in the loop. With --dyno the plant also offers its model's disturbances as inputs. Rec keeps the last minutes of every live signal (click the length to change it); Save ▾ › Live record writes them. Live settings in the Plant tab set the ramp-in and the references' full scales, saved with the system.

System library

Complete example systems, from a mass–spring–damper to a triple pendulum and a six-axis robot arm, each with its input, plant and controllers. Load a whole system, or only one part of it, for example the input of one system with the plant of another. Each card says in a few words what the system is and what to try; Details opens its full description, which the Plant tab keeps under About this system once it is loaded.

Files

The project is one JSON document, including how the display is set. Save it, open it, drop it on the page or paste it. Export ▾ in the header has the file keys: Save and Copy JSON; Export HTML writes this page with the project inside, to send to someone, Copy HTML copies it; and the downloads, the HIL plant and the MCP server, through which an agent works on this page with you.

Shown in a limited environment, such as a file preview that runs the page in a sandbox, a warning below the header stays, says what does not work there, and what to do: download the file and open it in your browser.

For agents

Everything a person does here an agent can do through window.loopTuner: loopTuner.help() returns this guide as data, loopTuner.api lists every method. (In the Loop Tuner repository, node cli.mjs help gives the command line's own help.)
